title: Your Bank and NBFC Team Up: Understanding Co-Lending
description: Banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) are now working together more closely to offer loans. This partnership, called co-lending, helps expand who .

faq.q: What kind of loans are typically co-lent?
faq.a: Co-lending is used for a variety of loans, including personal loans, home loans, vehicle loans, and especially loans to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and priority sector lending.

faq.q: Who do I repay the loan to?
faq.a: You will typically make repayments to the NBFC, which acts as the primary point of contact and handles the loan servicing. The NBFC then distributes the respective shares to the bank.

faq.q: Is my data safe with two financial entities?
faq.a: Yes, both the bank and the NBFC are regulated entities, and they must adhere to strict data privacy and security norms set by the RBI. The loan agreement specifies how data is shared and managed.

faq.q: What if there's a problem or grievance with my co-lent loan?
faq.a: The loan agreement will clearly state which entity is your main point of contact for grievances. You should first approach the NBFC, but both the bank and the NBFC are ultimately responsible for addressing your concerns.

faq.q: Does co-lending make the loan riskier for me as a borrower?
faq.a: No, co-lending does not make the loan riskier for you. In fact, the RBI's new guidelines aim to make the process more transparent and ensure clear responsibilities, providing better protection for borrowers.
